Overall, the main change driving this forecast package is the 
designation of Invest 91W by the JTWC and its subsequent upgrade to 
"Low" status. Currently, guidance does not develop 91W into a 
tropical cyclone until well west of the Marianas. During its 
disorganized stage, it likely will bring heavy rainfall to Guam over 
the next couple of days. Numerous locally heavy showers and isolated 
thunderstorms are expected for Guam Tuesday through Tuesday night, 
with high-end (50%) scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms for 
the CNMI. Model guidance ranges from 2 to 5 inches of rain across 
Guam through Wednesday evening and 1 to 3 inches of rain across the 
CNMI. See the Hydrology section for more details. 

As Invest 91W lifts off to the northwest, the monsoon trough looks 
to lift north of the region, shifting the active wet phase of the 
monsoon over the Marianas. See Tropical Weather Discussion for more
details. Currently, scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms 
through the period are forecasted. Shower coverage could increase 
across the region late this week and into the weekend depending on 
the setup monsoon trough. If Invest 91W tracks southerly, it could 
keep the monsoon trough further south over the Marianas. This would 
put under a col where island effect showers would be possible, 
similar to what we saw this past weekend. For now, the focus is heavy
rainfall on Tuesday and Wednesday, but if the Marianas see 
additional rainfall during the first half of the week, flooding 
concerns would increase heading into the weekend. &&

Marine...
Benign seas of 4 to 6 feet will continue before falling 1 to 2 feet 
during the second half of the week. Some choppy seas would be 
possible for Guam near heavier showers Tuesday and Wednesday. There 
is a moderate risk for rip currents along all reefs through Tuesday, 
and then for north and east facing reefs through Friday. 

Hydrology...
A Flash Flood Watch has been issued for Guam beginning 10 AM Tuesday 
until 10 PM Wednesday, calling for 2 to 5 inches of rain across Guam
during the timeframe. Much of Guam saw 2 to 4 inches of rain since 
this past Saturday, which has kept soils wet. An additional 2 to 5 
inches of rain would lead to flash flooding due to the wet 
antecedents. The main challenge is for the potential for Invest 91W 
to shift further west during its development, leading to less 
rainfall for Guam. Some of the recent 00z runs coming out after the 
forecast package have shown this shift. 

The main culprit of this shift is displacement of the low-level 
vorticity to the west of a Mid-Level Circulation (MLC). Models are 
keeping the MLC weak while quickly ramping up the low level vorticity
into a Low-Level Circulation (LLC). If the focus of convection 
shifts to the LLC, then rainfall amounts would be considerably lower
for Guam, keeping the risk for Flash Flooding low. Latest satellite 
trends seem to be favoring both with new towers going up along the 
developing LLC, but some towers have also developed along the
southern and eastern edges of the MLC. This adds uncertainty in the 
forecast. Currently, residents of Guam should prepare for heavy 
rainfall starting Tuesday as Invest 91W develops. Conditions will 
continue to be monitored through the night for significant changes. 

Tropical Systems...
A developing disturbance, Invest 91W, is found south of Guam, 
centered near 11N144E. 91W is now rated low, meaning that 
development into a significant tropical cyclone is not expected over
the next 24 hours, but will be possible over the next few days. 91W 
resides on the northern edge of the monsoon trough. Convection is 
sparse to the northern half of 91W, however, showers are increasing 
in this area. Convection remains very active on the south side. 
Invest 91W will slowly move northwest over the coming days.

For more information on Invest 91W, see bulletins issued by JTWC 
under WMO header ABPW10 PGTW.

Eastern Micronesia...
The main concern this afternoon is a strong monsoon surge over the
Marshall Islands, producing scattered showers and isolated
thunderstorms across Majuro with reports of gale-force winds and
gusts across the atoll. A short-term Gale Warning was issued for
majuro coastal waters through Tuesday at 3 AM ChST. The latest ASCAT
does show an area of 30+ knot winds south of and over Majuro. This 
surge will maintain near-gale to gale force winds and gusts through 
the night. Stronger gusts are likely with heavier showers. Winds 
should decrease early in the morning, falling below gale force around
3 AM ChST. 

For the remainder of the forecast, an overall unsettled pattern looks
to continue across Majuro into the weekend. For Pohnpei and Kosrae,
an overall dry pattern is in place and looks to continue through most
of the week. As the monsoon trough drifts a bit farther south late in
the week and over the weekend. expect a weak monsoon surge to
develop across Pohnpei and Kosrae, bringing increased convection to
